issues.legal_issue: A written demand notice served before an amendment remains sufficient for a later eviction suit when the amendment leaves the statutory notice requirement unchanged.
material_facts: The landlord served a written notice demanding rent arrears before the amendment took effect.
The tenant did not pay the demanded arrears within one month after service of the notice.
The amendment changed the provision governing eviction for arrears but did not change the provision requiring the pre-suit notice.
The landlord filed the eviction suit after the amendment took effect.
issues.conclusion: The earlier notice satisfied the statutory notice requirement; a fresh notice after the amendment was not required.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 12(2) and 12(3)(a) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, section 12(3)(a) refers to the notice required by section 12(2). Because the amendment did not alter section 12(2), a notice meeting that section’s requirements remained sufficient. The landlord was not required to tell the tenant what consequences would follow from non-payment.

rule.if: rent_arrears_eviction_suit and written_demand_before_suit and notice_met_demand_requirements and tenant_unpaid_within_notice_period and amendment_left_notice_requirement_unchanged

predicates.rent_arrears_eviction_suit: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding against a tenant on the ground of unpaid rent.
predicates.written_demand_before_suit: The landlord served the tenant with a written demand for rent before bringing the proceeding.
predicates.notice_met_demand_requirements: The written demand met the requirements that applied to a pre-suit rent notice.
predicates.tenant_unpaid_within_notice_period: The tenant did not pay the demanded rent within the period following service of the notice.
predicates.amendment_left_notice_requirement_unchan: A legislative amendment changed the eviction rule but left the pre-suit notice requirement unchanged.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings an eviction proceeding for rent arrears, a compliant written demand served before suit remains sufficient if the tenant does not pay within the notice period and the intervening amendment leaves the notice requirement unchanged.

issues.legal_issue: Under the amended arrears rule, a court must order eviction when the tenant has the requisite arrears and fails to pay within the notice period, even if the tenant pays before the decree and previously had an opportunity to pay later in the proceedings.
material_facts: The landlord’s written demand claimed rent arrears covering more than six months.
The tenant did not pay the demanded arrears within one month after receiving the notice.
The landlord filed the eviction suit after the amended provision took effect.
The tenant paid all the rent due before the trial court passed its decree.
The courts found that the case met the conditions for eviction under the amended arrears provision, and the Supreme Court dismissed the tenant’s appeal.
issues.conclusion: The amended provision governed the suit and required a decree for eviction; payment of the arrears before the decree did not prevent that result.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3)(a), read with sections 12(1) and 12(2) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, required eviction where there was no dispute about the standard rent or permitted increases, the tenant was in arrears for six months or more, and the tenant failed to pay within one month after the required notice. The amended provision applied because the suit was brought after the amendment took effect. The Court followed Kurban Hussen Sajuddin v. Ratikant Nilkant in treating “may” as “must” when the provision’s conditions were met. It distinguished the earlier rule discussed in Dayaram Kashiram Shimpi v. Bansilal Raghunath Marwari and Laxminarayan Nandkishore Shravagi v. Keshardev Baijnath Narsaria concerning payment during the suit or appeal. The provision did not confer a vested right to cure the default by paying later; even if such a right existed, it could not change the provision’s plain effect.

rule.if: rent_arrears_eviction_suit and no_dispute_about_rent_amount and arrears_at_least_six_months and compliant_notice_served and tenant_unpaid_within_notice_period and suit_after_amendment and tenant_paid_before_decree

predicates.rent_arrears_eviction_suit: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding against a tenant on the ground of unpaid rent.
predicates.no_dispute_about_rent_amount: The landlord and tenant did not dispute the amount of standard rent or permitted increases due.
predicates.arrears_at_least_six_months: The tenant owed rent arrears for six months or more.
predicates.compliant_notice_served: The landlord served the tenant with a written demand that met the applicable notice requirements.
predicates.tenant_unpaid_within_notice_period: The tenant did not pay the demanded rent within the period following service of the notice.
predicates.suit_after_amendment: The landlord brought the eviction proceeding after an amendment to the governing arrears rule took effect.
predicates.tenant_paid_before_decree: The tenant paid the rent due before the court entered its decree.

issues.definition: In a rent-arrears eviction proceeding brought after the governing amendment, the court must order eviction when the rent amount is undisputed, arrears reach the required duration, and the tenant fails to pay within the notice period, even if the tenant pays before the decree.
